text: In the cool dawn light of Northfold’s freight quarter, Corvane Motors on Tuesday began customer deliveries of its E3 electric van, a boxy workhorse aimed at local couriers and regional trades. The company says the model can travel up to 510 kilometres on a single charge, a figure that puts it ahead of earlier fleet vans introduced during the city’s post-petrol transition five years ago. Corvane chief engineer Lila Mern said the range was achieved through a denser battery pack and quieter motorway gearing, both developed at the firm’s Halewick test yard. Several small delivery firms had already placed orders, drawn by the E3’s promised low running costs and its ability to cover a full day’s routes without a midday charge.
